ATC group V is the catch-all letter of the classification [@whoccATCDDDIndex2026].
The notes below cover three of its nine level 2 codes: therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals, reversal agents and contrast media.

In 2002 Anton Bom and colleagues at Organon described a cyclodextrin that reverses rocuronium block by encapsulating the relaxant itself rather than acting on a receptor [@bomNovelConceptReversing2002].

| Level 2 code | Description |
| ---: | :--- |
| V01 | Allergens |
| V03 | All other therapeutic products |
| V04 | Diagnostic agents |
| V06 | General nutrients |
| V07 | All other non-therapeutic products |
| V08 | Contrast media |
| V09 | Diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals |
| V10 | Therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals |
| V20 | Surgical dressings |

: ATC V level 2 codes {#tbl-atc-v-lvl-2 tbl-colwidths="[20, 80]"}

## Modelling notes

**Endpoint.**
For therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals the driver is a physical quantity, the **absorbed dose** in Gy to tumour and organs at risk, reconstructed from serial post-infusion imaging rather than from a plasma concentration-time curve [@hebertAbsorbedDoseResponse2024].
In ^177^Lu-PSMA-617 therapy the lesion dose-response relationship is real but only moderate, Spearman rho about -0.3 [@grkovskiLesionAbsorbedDose2025].

**Decay is not clearance (V09, V10).**
Imaging measures activity, which falls by radioactive decay and by biological clearance together, so what is fitted is an effective half-life [@oliveiraAnalysisResidenceTime2022].
With few imaging time points the fit is unstable, and population fitting stabilises the time-integrated activity [@hardiansyahPopulationBasedMethod2021].

**Typical structure, reversal agents.**
Sugammadex encapsulates rocuronium and the complex is cleared by the kidney, so clearance of both falls in [renal impairment](/docs/concepts/clinpharm-studies/renal-impairment-studies/) [@staalsReducedClearanceRocuronium2010].
A population analysis nonetheless found renal function did not affect reversal time [@kleijnPopulationPharmacokineticPharmacodynamic2011].
The fitted model is complex formation using the *in vitro* dissociation constant, with effect driven by the fall in free rocuronium rather than by an E~max~ on sugammadex [@ploegerPharmacokineticPharmacodynamicModel2009].

**Reversal can wear off first (V03).**
The short duration of action of naloxone is a pharmacokinetic property, so reversal can wear off while the opioid is still present [@ngaiPharmacokineticsNaloxoneRats1976].
Judging a reversal dose therefore calls for a mechanistic model linking both drugs to ventilation [@yangMechanisticPharmacokineticPharmacodynamic2024].

**Contrast media, a pharmacokinetic problem.**
Iodinated X-ray media distribute differentially to organs and between normal and abnormal tissue, and are excreted largely unchanged, with a hepatic and biliary route that matters in renal impairment [@bourinOverviewClinicalPharmacokinetics1997].
Iohexol clearance is itself used as a measured GFR [@mohamedDiverseProtocolsMeasuring2024], and the practical question is the safe interval before the next study [@vandermolenWaitingTimesBetween2024].

**Mechanistic extrapolation (V10).**
PBPK has been applied in radiopharmaceutical therapy to predict time-integrated activity for treatment planning [@klettingPhysiologicallyBasedPharmacokinetic2015; @hardiansyahSensitivityAnalysisPhysiologically2016].
